title: autotrade — after the close: review, re-measure, adopt
_why: The only place a model touches trading, and it touches one thing: where to look.
The sequence is fixed here rather than left to an agent turn, because a run that
re-authors its own steps every night is a run whose steps can be wrong every night.
Step 0 walks the ladder from the ledger — no model involved, and it happens first so a
strategy that stopped working is demoted before anything new is considered.
Step 2 is the model's whole contribution: a search space. It reads what has already been
refused so it does not spend the night re-measuring ground that was covered.
Steps 3-6 measure. Step 7 adopts, and it receives the ranking, the planned runs and their
results as they came out of those steps — so the evidence never passes through the model.
19:30 KST on weekdays (the server is UTC), well after the close and after any late fills
have been reconciled by the intraday run.

pipeline.instruction:
You are given today's strategy review and the history of what has already been adopted or refused. Answer with a JSON object only — no prose, no explanation — describing where to search next for a trading rule.

Shape:
{"families":[...],"fast":[...],"slow":[...],"low":[...],"high":[...],"stopLossPct":[...],"takeProfitPct":[...],"holdout":0.3}

families is any of: ma-cross, ema-cross, rsi, bollinger, macd. The numeric fields are lists of parameter values to try; null is allowed in stopLossPct and takeProfitPct to mean "no stop". holdout is the fraction of history kept back for scoring.

Read the refusals in the history. A combination that was refused for too few trades will be refused again at the same parameters, so move somewhere else: slower parameters trade less, faster ones trade more. Keep the space under about 200 combinations — a wider search finds a better-looking result without finding a better rule.

confirmSymbols: Held out of the selection entirely. A rule is chosen on the other three and then measured
here; adoption refuses anything that was never put in front of these. This is the check
that caught a candidate winning on all three of its own symbols and then going 2/5 and
-45.7 points against buy & hold on symbols it had not seen.
symbol: What the adopted strategy actually trades. The sweep spans several symbols to show the
rule is not an artefact of one; the strategy then runs on the one we hold an account for.
whatTheModelCannotDo: Turn trading on, set the mode, arm real money, raise a limit, or write a result.
It proposes a region of parameter space. Everything that decides whether that region
produced something tradable is machine output flowing between steps.
